key_insight: Adapting pretrained DINOv3 improved fracture characterization in acoustic image logs over task-specific models trained from scratch with limited annotations.
engineering_relevance: Automated characterization of natural and drilling-induced tensile fractures can support rock mass assessment and in situ stress interpretation while reducing manual effort.
method: Fine-tune satellite-imagery-pretrained DINOv3 on annotated acoustic image logs.
Compare against U-Net, YOLOv8, and Swin Transformer models trained from scratch.
Test decoder architecture, fine-tuning strategy, and fracture-focused image enhancement.
evidence_signal: Using 80 annotated samples and evaluation on four held-out boreholes, adapted DINOv3 produced fracture parameter estimates comparable to human interpretation and fewer detection errors than the baselines.
watch_item: The performance advantage generally narrowed as training data decreased, and image enhancement did not consistently improve accuracy.
paper_title: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Fracture Characterization in Acoustic Image Logs
